scope: Rank pre-1877 primary map alternatives for individual stable physical features in Berchezoaia/Buteasa/Chioar, and distinguish primary documentary versus independently geodetic evidence.

hierarchy.known_source: eHarta scanner originals at 300dpi from university geography archives
hierarchy.reason: Would resolve sheet-specific print marginalia and source/survey/reprint annotations; BUT its 1924 printing date remains later than 1859 and does not by itself certify a legal boundary
hierarchy.noncontact_next_step: Check any already-public non-authenticated untrimmed scan or dataset mirror only, no form submission

hierarchy.class: Transylvania circa 1860–1872 Habsburg 2nd military survey, source 1:28,800
hierarchy.warning: Transylvania source sheets and the Kingdom of Hungary-only digital package are different provenances; do NOT infer that a Hungary sheet DVD covering 1819–1869 includes Transylvania. Historic triangulation and georeferencing uncertainty must be measured.
hierarchy.potential: Primary contemporaneous cartographic representation of churches and roads but lacks proven independent exact same-object ground mark for Chioar so far

hierarchy.warning: Original edition is independent as 1862 publication, but insufficient detail to identify a wooden church corner or the 1924 topographic spot height; later eHarta georeferencing used Austrian 1:200,000 maps, hence geodetically dependent.

hierarchy.class: MNL OL S75 No 82 administrative map, 1859 state photographed 1861
hierarchy.warning: Settlement shapes and heavy wavy administrative lines cannot be promoted as same-object river, wooden church vertex, or legal boundary without own legends and independent period proof.
Can screen structures existing in the 1924 image, not prove they existed on the same physical site in 1859; ~1.7 m per pixel is image sampling, not geodetic accuracy.

witness_and_landmark_crosswalk.claims: summary says 1800, narrative gives construction candidate 1751; consecration in 1839, collapse in 2019
witness_and_landmark_crosswalk.legal_result: Evidence supports pre-1859 monument existence but not certified original church point on 1859 map

witness_and_landmark_crosswalk.claims: heritage summary: 17th c; narrative: probably 1741; 1845 porch and door altered
witness_and_landmark_crosswalk.legal_result: Historic presence plausible but exact church footprint and map symbol not certified on pre1877 image

witness_and_landmark_crosswalk.claims: old wooden building moved to Codru Butesii in 1937, AFTER 1924 map
witness_and_landmark_crosswalk.legal_result: Hard chronological rejection of current site as 1859/1924 unchanged church vertex

required_per_point: Unique physical object sub-feature with documented survival at same site across both dates
Unique point observed on original period map at known source-image pixel coordinate, not merely centre of WMS crop
Independently surveyed, object-identical reference coordinate and positional uncertainty
Holdout points not fitted with model, enough noncollinear points for transform
